manifest.description: The final manifest, present once the job is complete.

manifest_digest.description: JCS SHA-256 of the final manifest.

Grade.description:
How strongly a claim is known, weakest to strongest.

The derived `Ord` is the semantics: `Asserted < Attested < Tested <
Checked`. A claim's grade can only rise as evidence accumulates.

The grade axis measures the *recheckability of the establishing procedure*,
not the authority of the speaker (`docs/spec/07-verdicts-and-llm-boundary.md`
§1). `Asserted` is the strongest word and the weakest evidence: authorial
fiat grades below a model's opinion because there is nothing to re-run — not
because the author is outranked. Authority lives in the valuation layer; the
lattice ranks evidence, the ledger ranks authority (charter koan 6).

oneOf.description: Grounded in will; there is nothing to re-run — author's word.
A stored model judgment: re-posable and contestable, not re-derivable.
Re-derives statistically — a battery over a committed spec and seed.
Re-derives exactly — anyone re-runs it and gets the same result.

InvariantOutcome.description: The outcome of sweeping one exact invariant over every trial of a run.

oneOf.description: The predicate held on every trial the run produced.
The predicate failed; the earliest witnessing trial and why.

detail.description: A domain-spoken account of the breach.

trial.description: The lowest-indexed trial at which the invariant broke.

oneOf.description:
The predicate's law was never enforced this run, so nothing was actually
swept — an `affine bounded` resource whose symbolic cap never resolved to a
number (or a resource with no declared law) can neither hold nor break. A
deferred outcome is reported honestly and MUST NOT read as a held pass: an
unenforced law that showed `held` would forge a verified grade
(`docs/spec/07-verdicts-and-llm-boundary.md` — grades are honest).

reason.description: Why the law was not enforced (the unresolved-cap reason).

InvariantVerdict.description: The verdict of one declared invariant over a run, graded [`Grade::Checked`].

grade.description:
Always [`Grade::Checked`] — an invariant is an exact, re-derivable sweep.

Private: the only writer is [`new`](InvariantVerdict::new), which stamps
the type-level constant, so no struct literal outside this module can
forge a grade. Read it with [`grade`](InvariantVerdict::grade).
Deserialization re-checks it against the constant, so a forged wire value
is rejected rather than admitted.

invariant.description: The name of the declared invariant this settles.

outcome.description: Held, or violated with the witnessing trial.

MetricEstimate.description:
A Monte-Carlo estimate of one declared metric, graded [`Grade::Tested`].

The [`sum`](MetricEstimate::sum) and [`sum_of_squares`](MetricEstimate::sum_of_squares)
are the exact integer sufficient statistics — the portable, replayable core of
the estimate. The [`mean`](MetricEstimate::mean) and
[`half_width`](MetricEstimate::half_width) are derived conveniences (a 95%
normal-approximation interval); trust the counts, read the interval.

grade.description:
Always [`Grade::Tested`] — a metric is a statistical estimate, forever.

Private: the only writer is [`from_counts`](MetricEstimate::from_counts),
which stamps the type-level constant, so no struct literal outside this
module can forge a grade. Read it with [`grade`](MetricEstimate::grade).
Deserialization re-checks it against the constant, so a forged wire value
is rejected rather than admitted.

half_width.description: Half-width of the 95% normal-approximation interval; `0.0` below 2 trials.

mean.description: The point estimate: `sum / trials`, or `0.0` when no trial contributed.

metric.description: The name of the declared metric this estimates.

sum.description: The exact sum of the observed per-trial values.

sum_of_squares.description: The exact sum of squares of the observed values (for the variance).

trials.description: The number of trials that contributed an observation.

RunManifest.description:
The committed record of a battery run.

Serialization is deterministic: declaration-ordered fields, `Vec`s in the
battery's own declaration order (never a hash map), so
[`canonical_bytes`](RunManifest::canonical_bytes) is byte-stable and two runs
of the same battery — straight through or resumed from a checkpoint — produce
identical bytes.

Deserialization is guarded: each grade field validates itself against its
type-level constant as it is read (see
[`MetricEstimate`]/[`InvariantVerdict`]), so a hostile record with a forged
grade (a metric stamped `checked`, an invariant stamped `tested`) is
*rejected* at `deserialize` time in release, not merely in a debug assertion.
Combined with the private grade fields — which block a struct-literal forge at
compile time — the SIM-1 oracle cannot be evaded.

battery_digest.description: The digest of the battery that produced this run.

checkpoint_lineage.description:
The trial-count boundaries at which the run's state was assembled — its
checkpoint lineage. `[trials]` for an uninterrupted run; the full cadence
(e.g. `[k, 2k, …, trials]`) for a checkpointed one, reconstructed
identically whether the run was interrupted and resumed or not.

invariants.description: Per-invariant exact verdicts, in the battery's declaration order.

metrics.description: Per-metric Monte-Carlo estimates, in the battery's declaration order.

seed.description: The master seed the run drew every choice from.

trials.description: The number of trials folded into this manifest.

SimulateJobStatus.description: A durable simulation job's lifecycle state.

oneOf.description: At least one checkpoint has been committed.
A final manifest has been committed.
